modern: Regret is a kind of self-reproach for having neglected something useful; but what is good must be something useful, and the perfectly good man should look after it. But no such man would ever regret having refused any sensual pleasure. Pleasure, then, is neither good nor useful.

explained.summary: A short argument that pleasure isn’t really good. Regret means blaming yourself for missing something useful, and anything good is useful. Yet no good person regrets turning down a pleasure. So pleasure is neither good nor useful. Pleasure, for a Stoic, is neither good nor bad in itself.
